These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

#1526. GdS: Linear structure and a strong work force – what Krösche is likely to implement at Milan

AC Milan are expected to hire Markus Krösche in the next few weeks, and a report has looked a little more at his work today.

Between Eintracht Frankfurt and Milan, there are plenty of differences. From the finances available to how they’re spent, even to the way in which the structure of the club ticks over. So, Krösche will have to learn with the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it won’t be a one way street, with the Diavolo needing to learn plenty too.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, Krösche methods are very linear; it’s about arriving and leaving at the right time, having the knowledge to enter and the courage to step away when the time is right.

His belief is that the club will always hold more weight than the manager, which has been shown in the past few months by Gerry Cardinale and there is no shortage of exciting signings on his CV.

What is also worth remembering is that he’s not one to step away from his methods. In 2022, he was given a chance to sign Cristiano Ronaldo. However, it didn’t make sense for him or Frankfurt, so they never made their move.

If it happens his way, Timmo Hardung will arrive alongside the German. The pair met at RB Leipzig and their relationship has only grown since then and Krösche eventually led a team of 70 people at Frankfurt. In other words, he won’t be out of place at the top of the Milan football organisation.

Gazzetta even suggests that it’s ‘no secret’ that his desire is to move to Italy to work under Krösche once again. Given their successes together, it makes sense why all parties are hoping to keep that relationship under the same roof.

#1525. Spalletti apologises after Genoa defeat leaves Juventus level with Napoli on 14 points

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Genoa needed little time to break through, and Ehizibue was the man to do it. His goal ended a 504-minute run without a Genoa goal against Juventus in Serie A, going back to an Albert Gudmundsson strike on 15 December 2023, Sportmediaset reported.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

The coach did not hide from the performance. His team were beaten in every area of the pitch and must improve physically and in their fighting spirit, Spalletti told the club’s website. In his press conference he pointed to a lack of physical impact and to lost duels.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

The evening got worse elsewhere. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza, with goals from Højlund, Politano, Rafa Marín and De Bruyne. Their coach, Massimiliano Allegri, watched from the stands. He was serving a two-match ban picked up against Roma.

Spalletti described Napoli as a very strong team. Both sides sit well behind the top of the table, so the meeting carries weight for each.

#1523. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1521. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

#1520. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

#1519. How Real Madrid gave in to the crazy demands of the JJ Gabriel file

Real Madrid is therefore the big winner in the battle to enlist the very young (16 years old) JJ Gabriel. It has already been a few weeks since Casa Blanca gained the upper hand over other European clubs such as PSG, but also Bayern Munich and FC Barcelona. This race led to overbidding, while the attacking midfielder did everything to leave Manchester United where he was considered the greatest hope of the training center. He was even called up by Michael Carrick to participate in the pre-season.

He probably expected to get some playing time in the first team but ultimately settled for the reserves. To his great dismay. There is undoubtedly something other than a story of playing time under this file because it is difficult to guarantee minutes to a particularly young player when you are called Real Madrid or PSG. MU will only receive around 400,000 euros for its nugget, in training compensation. JJ Gabriel has never signed a professional contract. This is also what attracted attention for such a precocious phenomenon.

We learn today in Sport the reasons why Casa Blanca got their hands on it. The club from the Spanish capital accepted the family’s demands. They are considerable for a player of only 16 years old. The overall operation is estimated at €15 million between salary, bonuses, commissions and the check to be paid to MU. Faced with such sums, Bayern Munich and Barça said no, refusing to enter into this economic game. Even the Red Devils preferred to withdraw from the file even though they had a serious advantage.

This morning, the English nugget poses with the front page of Marca being dedicated to him. “Can I keep it?» is written on the pro-Madrilenian daily. In addition to the particularly high offer, Real presented him with a road map to start from Castilla before making the jump to the first team. The attacking midfielder should join one of the youth categories in January 2027. Finally, management was also able to count on the support and entourage of Jude Bellingham to convince him to sign. This obviously had its little effect.

#1518. Tare discusses new Milan direction, limitations in his role and ‘jealousy’: “Better late than never”

Igli Tare has spoken without holding anything back about his time at AC Milan, explaining his frustration with several things.

When Tare arrived, many Milan fans were happy to see someone with Serie A experience oversee the project and whilst his first season didn’t end how anyone had hoped, he wasn’t seen as a major issue.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, when it was announced that he was part of a complete overturning of the management, there was a bit of a surprise, even if it did feel inevitable at one point.

With the overhaul of changes in the summer, one does wonder what Tare would have done differently, especially with suggestions that his hands were tied in the mercato last season. Nevertheless,

Speaking on Sky Sport’s ‘Calcio Unplugged’, Igli Tare revealed all to Gianluca Di Marzio and Stefano Borghi in an in-depth interview about his time with the Diavolo, as Radio Rossonera has relayed.

“Today is the first time I’ve spoken out after all these months. The wound of not having reached the Champions League is still enormous, and since I arrived at Milan – also questioning myself with the type of contract I signed – the objective couldn’t be only the Champions League; otherwise I wouldn’t have understood where I was.”

“It was great because he was the one who convinced me. He had such a huge desire to join Milan. I wanted to video chat before going to see him because I couldn’t believe it. But after five minutes, I knew in my head that he was the player Milan really lacked.

“Not just because of his qualities, but as a man and as a figure that that team didn’t have. He never said no. A photo with a child, an autograph, a meeting, talking to someone… He never said no. These are the things that humility is key to in life.

“I’m proud to have brought a great champion to Milan. In my opinion, if he wants, he can play another two seasons without any problem. He never missed a training session. Sometimes we were the ones to stop him because he was always there, ready. Loving football at that age is truly an honour.”

Is it a characteristic of the champion or is it a generational issue? Today’s champions seem to have a different mentality:

“Today we live in the age of social media. At 16, you’re already a footballer who can earn millions of euros. Living this way, you have the problem of not only managing a player, who is still a child, but you have to manage the business they bring with them: family, agents, girlfriends…

“These are obstacles that didn’t exist back then. We were a generation that played in the streets. Back then, our parents beat us to get us to come home. Today, however, it’s to get them out of the house because they spend all day in front of computers.

“This aspect has been lost a bit, but it’s our fault. Education and discipline are the key to success.”

Fullkrug. He performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

“It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund.

“There are situations where, for a player, even a very important one, it matters how you feel. If you feel appreciated, valued, taken into consideration… When you play for a club like Milan, the weight of the shirt is completely different than when you play for other clubs.

“You feel it from the first day you join. I had no doubt that he could be what he’s demonstrating now.”

“We tried to sign him back in June. We made a first attempt. In the final days of the transfer window, another important name we tried to sign was Akanji. The Champions League was crucial for both of them. They turned him down, not because of the club’s importance, but because he wasn’t playing in the Champions League.

“Then the opportunity arose again at the end of August for Rabiot. Defeat against Cremonese? No, we had already decided to bring him. It was just a matter of contract details.”

“It was difficult for us because we decided to change the formation five days before the transfer window closed. Switching from a 4-3-3 to a three-man defense meant we were having a really hard time finding a quality player in the last five days.

“We were a bit unlucky, first with the Akanji story and then with Liverpool’s Joe Gomez… Guehi’s move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool fell through, and at the last minute they—we already had the deal ready, we were just waiting for this to happen—made a step back. And to avoid being left without a central defender at the last minute, we signed Odogu as a promising player.”

On not being able to reach the Champions League and not being able to continue his work at Milan…

“This is the first time today, after all these months, that I’ve spoken about this… The wound of not reaching the Champions League is still enormous. I think that from the first day I arrived at Milan, even in the way I signed—I questioned myself with the type of contract.

“I said, ‘If I have to come only for the Champions League objective, then I don’t understand where I’ve come from.’ Milan has a different story. I had to go through a trial. The disappointment is that those who run the club didn’t understand how much time people needed, which is now being done, rightly so.

“That is to say, it takes several transfer sessions to get a competitive team ready to win. At the beginning, I felt the responsibility to put the pieces together immediately, because after the defeat in the Coppa Italia final the year before, there were some important signs.

“I didn’t know where to start. But I think we did an important job last summer, we sold for a lot and also signed 10 new players. Then you need time to integrate, learn new philosophies and create a cohesive group, hungry to win.

“Until March-April, we were a group with difficulties, but we were at the top of the table. Then in the last 10 matchdays, we had a mental breakdown, also due to other external dynamics, which I don’t want to discuss here, which had a significant impact.

“Internal or external dynamics? External to the team. But we also have some blame: myself first and foremost, along with Max [Allegri].

“We had to be a little more attentive to certain dynamics. We needed to be more present with the team to ultimately lead them to the final result. Isolation is the wrong word; I don’t believe in these things. I believe in teamwork; I believe in cohesion: from the club to the team.

“When this happens, you transmit it to the team. When these situations become possible, you could also see it in the team’s results, because the players are very attentive. Sometimes we think they have other interests, but they pay attention to everything that comes out. They follow everything very carefully and transmit it.

“Instilling serenity… How can you convey serenity? When, in difficult moments, you show that you believe in the project more than before. Sometimes I missed this feeling, a lack of something that could give us the final push.”

But despite this, did you think you could continue? Does this farewell after only a year feel like a stab in the back?

“Look, I would have asked for a round table where we could all sit down together and analyze everything. Then they could have just said ‘no, thanks’… But I respect the decision they made. I accept it with great regret, but I’ve never questioned it because there’s someone above me who has to decide, including for the fate of the club.

“And when they decide to take a different path, you have to accept it. I know things could have gone differently, even much better. I’ll always be a Milan fan, even after an experience like that.”

Was AC Milan a team that needed the constant presence of a manager or coach to avoid letting itself go as it later did?

“The feeling I had at the beginning was that this leadership was a bit lacking. The arrival of Modric—and another of our goals was also Granit Xhaka, Leverkusen’s captain—was precisely to bring real players into the group, with important characteristics and capable of leading others.

“Granit didn’t arrive; Luka arrived, who has a different way of being a leader: he does it in silence and with his attitude on the pitch. I had the opportunity to meet Mike Maignan: an extraordinary guy, a soul who cares deeply about the AC Milan shirt.

“Gabbia is another extraordinary guy; he lives for this club. Rabiot too… His experience spoke for itself. The great disappointment is that I expected something more in terms of responsibility and leadership from Pulisic: he’s a top-class player with unquestionable qualities. But in terms of performance, things happened that I had never experienced in my career…

“Like Gimenez: an extraordinary guy with numbers that spoke for themselves; for a year he failed to score a goal. Then it happened that Pulisic didn’t score for six months. He scored a goal. Then Leao didn’t score for four months.

“Situations that are hard to come by in football have happened… It can happen that you don’t score for a month, two months, but that long a period of time also affected the team’s final performance.

“Losing a match against Cagliari the way we did, 2-1, I think was the worst match of my life. The feeling and the disappointment I felt towards the fans in the stadium that night is something I will never forget for the rest of my life.”

If Cardinale had been the Cardinale he is today, the one who is also physically present, would you still be AC ​​Milan’s DS?

“I can’t answer that question; he has to answer it. I can say that I remember when the Jashari negotiations were going on… I had just landed in Rome and I was very pleased when he called me because he wanted to understand what was happening in that negotiation.

“I explained all the dynamics to him and I really liked that he said, ‘Anything you need, if you have to spend a little more, let me know because I’m here.’ Then during that process I never had the chance to talk to him, even intentionally.

“There were other people above me who I never wanted to bypass. I never had a direct relationship with him, and the possibility of a discussion would have helped everyone. Not me, but everyone. By putting all the problems and dynamics on the table, we could have resolved things much sooner. But I think it’s a new experience for Cardinale.

“He’s had experience in other sports in America. Now he’s done something important, taking responsibility and putting his face on the line. I would have preferred to have had that presence even when I was there because it would have been very useful. But for the Milan, better late than never.

“Now, for better or worse, he will make his own decisions and responsibilities. I think that for him, too, the best interests of Milan come first.”

Was Leao a problem or a resource in your mind?

“I knew him from the outside. When I had the chance to meet him in person, I thought he was an extraordinary guy. I truly loved him as a person, like everyone else. But he was the player from whom we all expected something more. I think football was no longer a priority for him. That’s the key to understanding him.”

“I think a bit about his life outside of football. Music, fashion, things… But I never doubted the sense of belonging he had towards Milan. You could sense that he loved playing for Milan and was suffering from not performing.

“He had many physical problems… First a calf, then a bit of pubalgia… He always played with his hands under control. I always tried to have individual conversations with him more than with any other Milan player.

“Every time I spoke to him, I left with a positive feeling. I sensed that he wanted to. But sometimes wanting isn’t enough.”

Was there a chance that Leao would leave during your summer too?

“A concrete offer never came for him. Regarding the other transfers, it’s not just Tare’s job. When I arrived – even at Lazio – I was a bit alone, but I tried to involve all the members of the club to give him the importance he needed to build a sense of belonging and responsibility. I think I did a very good job, together with Furlani, Ibra, and Moncada.

“We achieved significant sales figures, in a year when we weren’t even in the Champions League. Thanks to the work we did last summer, investments were made this year, with the money we had at the time. I really believe in teamwork.

“I said it even before the Coppa Italia match against Bari; I asked to speak to convey the importance of the work of the people within the club because it was right that way. Then afterwards, it’s human…

“They were coming off a bad year, when two cumbersome figures like Tare and Allegri arrive, and everyone was talking about Tare and Allegri, some disappointment was understandable. I understood the feeling they had, but I could… There was little to do about it.

“For me, it was a new path, a new opportunity. It was essential to work as a team and present ourselves as a real company.”

#1517. Spalletti calls job question provocative and vows no step back before Napoli

Luciano Spalletti struck a defiant tone on the eve of Juventus-Napoli, a game seen as a must-win. He also backed the club's response to the defeat at Genoa, including a squad retreat.

Spalletti made his stance clear on the eve of Juventus-Napoli. Anyone expecting him to retreat even slightly, he warned, should expect something different.

Sunday’s game is at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti said the side want to win back the respect that has been taken from them. Several outlets say his job is on the line.

The build-up has been shaped by the club’s response to the defeat at Genoa. Ehizibue scored in the 12th minute and Baldanzi in the 28th. After a long meeting between chief executive Giovanni Carnevali and the squad, Spalletti announced a retreat. The team would stay at the Continassa from Friday evening until the Napoli game.

Spalletti called Carnevali’s address perfect and said he had hit the right notes. He has never been keen on training-camp retreats. In these circumstances, though, he said one could help the group become more compact again.

The coach also played down any need for public backing. He needs no reassurance from the club, only a reaction from the team, Eurosport reported. He added that he is not asking his players for anything beyond their capabilities.

After nine rounds, this season’s tally trails the 15 Juventus had at the same stage last season and the 17 under Motta in 2024/25. It is above the 13 under Allegri in 2022/23, according to Tuttosport.

Recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. A 2-0 win at Lecce and the loss at Genoa complete the run. Two of those five games ended in defeat, and Juventus failed to score in both.

Napoli arrive without their coach. The Serie A sporting judge banned Massimiliano Allegri for two matches over disrespectful remarks to the officials in the 3-3 draw with Roma. The ban covers the Monza and Juventus games.

Spalletti also offered a hint on selection. He said Edon Zhegrova and Jeremie Boga would come on in the second half even if they did not start.

There is little time to recover whatever the result. Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League on Thursday 5 November at 21:00.

#1516. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1515. “Important to take time” – Gabbia admits January return is possible with right precautions

Matteo Gabbia has admitted that he could return to the field in January for AC Milan, but he doesn’t want to rush back.

It has been a difficult season for Milan, at least where injuries are concerned. In defence, they have had issues reminiscent of the 2023/24 season, where Gabbia had to be brought back from his loan spell at Villarreal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, though, it seems Gerry Cardinale is going to go down a different route and spend to help Ruben Amorim with his defensive options. Indeed, there have been plenty of rumours about recruitments at the back.

However, Gabbia could again be a key returnee in January, with him hoping to return from injury early in the new year.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) – at an event organised by the Milan Foundation at Milan’s “Arturo Toscanini” secondary school, where they met with several children with disabilities – Gabbia discussed the importance of the event, as well as his recovery.

“It’s wonderful, very enjoyable to spend hours with them. It’s also beautiful to see how they manage to create a group, something that really shows the importance of teamwork, the importance of friendship, even among themselves.

“We’re happy; we thank Fondazione Milan for the project, which is always beautiful and important: we’re happy to be a part of it and we’re enjoying the afternoon.”

Are you able to rejoin the group in January?

“Yes, that could be the time: we’re trying to work hard and do everything as best we can. I obviously have to thank the physiotherapists and the doctor because we’re really doing everything we can every day to try to heal the injury and get back on the pitch feeling good.

“It’s definitely been an unlucky season for me so far: I don’t want it to happen again or for any recurrences, so it’s also important to take the right time, get back in shape, and support the team right now.”

“Although it’s bad for the team that there are so many injured players, we’re together right now, supporting each other and trying to encourage each other through therapy, gym work, and the entire recovery process. Therefore, we’re trying to work as a team this week too, to overcome all the players’ injuries.

“From a personal standpoint, I’m trying to take this time calmly, in the sense that these things are part of sport, part of life, and not all moments are the same.

“This is certainly a difficult time, but it still allows me to stay close to the team, to try to lend my support, even in the good and bad times. That’s what I’m doing, in addition to obviously doing what I can to try to return as soon as possible and make my contribution on the pitch.”

How do you explain the team’s ups and downs?

“I think it’s something we need to get our heads around; we need to understand the importance of every game.

“The other day I heard our coach give an interview in which he said something important: we need to understand that every game, when you don’t win, is taken as a defeat, a heavy defeat. We need to truly understand the importance of every game and approach training to prepare 100%, as best as possible, for every match.

“Therefore, I think this is room for improvement, but I see a group that is really eager to improve, to work, and as a result, I’m sure we’ll be able to fix this flaw as well.

“Although we’ve had a good start to the year in the league and less so in the Europa League, we have plenty of time to improve and have a strong year.”

#1514. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1513. Taking instructions from a schoolboy and showing class at half-pace... William Saliba made impressive injury comeback for Arsenal Under-21s - now he faces fight to take Ezri Konsa's spot, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026

It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

But his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday

His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

It was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

There is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

Saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

He returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines

Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa

Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight

It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

One particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

His afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence

The 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

Few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

Arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

#1512. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.
