Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

#1511. “It is an honour” – Yormark speaks after Milan Sport & Entertainment CEO appointment

Earlier today, AC Milan were introduced to a new name, thanks to the creation of a new company: Milan Sports & Entertainment.

The international break is never really a period of major news, yet Milan broke that spell today. Indeed, RedBird Capital Partners published a statement about a new company formed to oversee all of the Rossoneri’s business.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A centralised company that would allow everything Diavolo to be kept in one place is a major step forward for the club and city. San Donato was mentioned as an important focus for the new company, but the headline will remain the footballing operation.

To help with the project, Gerry Cardinale – who spoke about the decision – has appointed Brett Yormark to be the CEO of the company and reports suggest that he will join in January.

Speaking today, via MilanNews, Yormark admitted it was an honour to be part of the Milan family.

“It is an honour and a privilege to take on this role in a city with Milan’s history and passion for sports. I understand the responsibility that comes with leading an organisation tied to institutions that mean so much to their fans and the communities they serve.

“Throughout my career, I have helped evolve sports organisations, expand their reach, and create new opportunities. I look forward to leveraging this experience to realise RedBird’s vision for MSE.

“I am thrilled to work alongside Gerry, RedBird, and our colleagues in Milan to transform this vision into concrete, lasting results.”

#1510. McKennie ruled out of AZ trip with adductor fatigue as Alajbegović and Cabal return

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

A short rest should be enough, because the injury is fatigue rather than a tear, Sky Sport Italia reported. He should be back for the league. The problem is in his right adductor. The medical staff will check him again before Thursday, ANSA said.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. At 19 years and 41 days, the teenager has set a new mark: no non-Italian scorer in a Serie A meeting of these two clubs has been younger.

His knee knock has already cleared up. Cabal made way for Andrea Cambiaso after 83 minutes with cramp. That is put down to him not having started a game for some time. He will be available in Alkmaar.

Their return matters because the squad is badly stretched. Seven players are on the long-term injury list. Rugani, Zhegrova, Ekhator and Milik were left out of the UEFA squad. Losing McKennie, who can play several positions, leaves Spalletti with even fewer options for the trip to the Netherlands.

The match at AZ kicks off at 21:00 CET on 5 November. It is Matchday 4 of the league phase. Juventus have two wins and a draw so far.

AZ will be hard to break down at home. Their last home defeat in Europe was 4-1 to Aston Villa in the Conference League in October 2023.

Juventus arrive in good scoring form. They have nine goals in this season’s Europa League. Only Benfica, with ten, have scored more. That is Juventus’s best total after three games of a European campaign since 1999/2000.

⚪⚫ Kerim Alajbegović's first league goal for Juventus ✅#UEL | @juventusfc pic.twitter.com/GPcn8KJZga

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) November 2, 2026

History against Dutch opposition also offers encouragement. Juventus are unbeaten in three previous Europa League games against Dutch clubs, with two wins and one draw. They scored seven goals and conceded one in those matches.

McKennie’s absence will shape the midfield in Alkmaar, but the focus will quickly shift to his recovery. His place for the next league game is in doubt. Juventus visit Fiorentina on Matchday 11, on Sunday 8 November 2026 at 20:45.

#1509. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

That had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

An almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

#1508. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

“I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

“He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

“It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. #1507. Soccer hooligans descend on Australia: Wild footage shows horde of fans smashing cars and damaging property

Published: 03:01 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:38 EST, 11 November 2026

Shocking footage of soccer fans after a match has reignited complaints about public safety, following previous warnings repeated violence was putting families at risk.

Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

Other footage filmed from across the road shows young people confronting fans in the street, with the group spread across the footpath and roadway outside nearby businesses.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions, as well as damaged fences and other property. Supporters allege the material documents a recurring problem involving the same group and have demanded bans and stronger security measures.

The footage prompted calls for bans and renewed criticism of matchday security, with supporters alleging genuine fans face strict enforcement over minor issues while more serious behaviour goes unchecked.

'The same group of troublemakers causing chaos and mobbing random people', one fan posted on social media platform X.

Young people crowd around a parked white car and aggressively rock it near HBF Park in footage that has sparked anger among Perth Glory supporters

Supporters allege genuine fans are being left feeling unsafe at Perth Glory matches

Tagging Perth Glory, they added: 'It's time you do something about it. People have had enough.'

The supporter also called for individuals to be banned and, in a subsequent post, alleged nearby property had been damaged.

WA Police, Perth Glory and A-Leagues have all been contacted for comment.

Perth-based football podcast and digital channel The Far Post Perth shared the original post, adding its own demand for intervention.

'Not a good look at all and something needs to be done about the problem at this point, genuine supporters are being impacted,' the account wrote.

One commenter alleged the group had been moving through the venue during the match while being followed by security and police.

'This is the mob that was walking back and forth all game with security/police following,' they wrote.

'We don't need this at HBF Park. It makes many people feel unsafe when these wannabe thugs just shove their way through.'

Another video shows young people confronting fans on the street outside nearby businesses

Photographs of damaged fences and other property have fuelled calls for stronger action

The person who posted the footage claimed that 'after the game the police and security were nowhere to be seen'.

They also shared a separate video from February, alleging it showed an earlier confrontation involving the same group.

The February post had complained about people attending matches in The Bay supporter area and allegedly fighting with other young spectators.

The complaints follow a strongly worded statement issued last year by supporter groups The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth, which demanded sanctions after a separate incident outside Gate 2 during the second half of a match at HBF Park.

The groups said they were aware of footage circulating online and distanced themselves from those involved, alleging physical confrontations had become a recurring problem.

'We want to make it absolutely clear that those involved are not fans and do not represent our supporter groups, our values, or the wider football community,' their joint statement read.

'These individuals consistently attend matches with the sole intention of causing problems rather than supporting the team, and their behaviour is completely unacceptable.'

The statement alleged confrontations had occurred in active supporter areas and the Eastern family stand, extending the groups' concerns beyond the stadium's most vocal sections.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions

'In almost every single game, they have caused physical confrontations in both the Active areas, and in some cases the Eastern family stand too, and it is deeply frustrating that this behaviour continues without meaningful consequences,' the groups said.

They alleged the behaviour was damaging the experience of supporters who attended matches to follow Perth Glory.

The groups also accused matchday security provider NPB Security of failing to respond adequately to incidents.

Their criticism included allegations that a rotating contingent of inexperienced security staff was being deployed and that personnel were unable or unwilling to intervene when serious problems arose.

'The lack of accountability from NPB Security is unacceptable and has undermined the safety of the matchday environment,' the statement read.

'Warnings and passive responses are clearly not working.'

The groups called for bans and other sanctions, warning that further incidents could affect spectators and people working at the ground.

'Without firm action, including bans and real consequences, these so-called 'fans' will continue to put genuine supporters, families, and staff at risk.'

They urged the club and stadium authorities to identify those responsible and impose firm sanctions.

Their earlier warning has been followed by fresh complaints about how security rules are enforced at Perth Glory matches.

'Meanwhile security go OTT about bottled water in the shed or actual fans taking t-shirts off,' one supporter wrote in response to the latest footage.

Another commenter similarly complained that removing a shirt in the supporter bay could result in ejection, while alleging people involved in violence escaped consequences.

The Far Post Perth also challenged a response that dismissed the latest incident as 'kids being kids'.

'Kids being kids is vandalising other people's property? Interesting,' the account replied, referring to the allegations of property damage.

However, one person responding to the original footage questioned whether those shown in the street were Perth Glory supporters.

'In the second video, the person filming is standing where the stadium is. These idiots look like they are walking from the other side of the road,' the commenter wrote.

'Are we sure they are even Glory fans? Or just troublemakers.'

The person who uploaded the footage insisted they were, although the posts do not establish that the same individuals were involved in each of the incidents raised by commenters.

The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth had made their position on violence explicit in their earlier appeal for action.

'Violence, fighting, and antisocial behaviour have no place in football,' they said.

'HBF Park, The Shed, The Bay and all areas of the ground should be a safe and welcoming environment for all supporters, families, players, and staff.'

#1506. Juventus extend Elimoghale to 2029 as Carnevali puts youth sector at the centre

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

The club announced Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November. That was the same day chief executive Giovanni Carnevali addressed shareholders at the Allianz Stadium. He called for a single project covering the first team, the Next Gen and the youth sector.

Elimoghale has come through every level of the club’s academy. He has been at Juventus since childhood. This season he began playing professional football in Serie C.

The NEC fixture was the opening matchday of the Europa League league phase. Spalletti named three Next Gen players because the first team was hit by injuries, Tuttosport reported. Pagnucco and Owusu joined Elimoghale. All three were in a European squad for the first time.

Elimoghale did not get on the pitch in the comfortable win. He stayed on the bench as an unused substitute, alongside Vicario, Pinsoglio and Pagnucco.

Back in Serie C, his minutes have been mixed. In a 5-3 home defeat to Albinoleffe on the sixth matchday, he tried two long-range shots. One went just wide. Goalkeeper Baldi saved the other. At Trento on the 11th matchday, he replaced Leone in the 70th minute of a 2-1 defeat. The match came in Serie C Group A. He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Carnevali said the club must bring its youth sector back to the level of recent years. He added that Juventus must keep trying to improve it. Securing a home-grown forward for the long term is consistent with that message.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

Aggiornamento della lista UEFA: Jeff Ekhator subentra a Manuel Locatelli. pic.twitter.com/I3Mi1W0PSB

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 3, 2026

For Elimoghale, the wider picture is a first team still short of bodies. Coaches have already turned to the Next Gen once in Europe. A new long-term deal means the club has secured one of those options.

The squad remains stretched heading into the next round of European fixtures. McKennie is suffering from muscle fatigue and will miss the Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar. Alajbegovic and Cabal are expected to be available in the Netherlands. The trip comes with the European squad list already being reshaped.

#1503. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1502. Koopmeiners scores at former club as Juventus beat AZ 2-1 despite trailing on expected goals

Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on a night when Teun Koopmeiners faced his old club, even though the hosts dominated the expected-goals count. The result strengthens their league-phase position ahead of Sunday's Serie A trip to Fiorentina.

The trip to Alkmaar returned Teun Koopmeiners to his former club. His brother Peer was in the AZ side that Juventus then held off. UEFA picked out the family meeting in its matchday 4 round-up.

Koopmeiners opened the scoring in the 19th minute from a Kolo Muani pass. Kolo Muani doubled the lead in the 37th minute, with Nick Woltemade credited with the assist, and Juventus led 2-0 at half-time. Kolo Muani earned a rating of 8.61 from the data provider, with Koopmeiners on 8.2.

AZ pulled one back in the 88th minute. Mexx Meerdink scored from an Elijah Dijkstra assist. The hosts could not find an equaliser in the remaining minutes.

The home side had 56% of possession. They completed 523 passes to Juventus’s 378. Eleven of AZ’s attempts were blocked, against three of Juventus’s.

Both teams put three shots on target. Vicario made two saves for Juventus. AZ’s expected goals total points to the chances the hosts created without converting them.

The figures are consistent with a Juventus side defending a first-half lead. Spalletti’s team committed 20 fouls to AZ’s 13. Andrea Cambiaso, Jeff Ekhator and Juan Cabal were booked for Juventus. Wesley Hoedt was the only AZ player shown a yellow card. Damian Sylwestrzak refereed the match.

The victory was Spalletti’s second in a row in all competitions, following the league win over Napoli. It came after a run that included a 0-2 defeat to Genoa and a 0-3 loss to Lazio. Koopmeiners now has four goals for Juventus in all competitions in 2026, one more than the three he scored for the club in 2025, Sky Sport Italia noted.

For AZ, the result was a third straight defeat in all competitions. Losses to Ajax and Twente came before Thursday’s game.

This season’s league phase has 36 clubs, and each plays eight different opponents. It ends on Thursday 28 January 2027. Juventus host Omonia Nicosia on 26 November at 21:00 CET, while AZ travel to Sparta Praha. Juventus then visit Hapoel Beer-Sheva on 10 December and Ferencváros on 21 January 2027, both at 18:45 CET. They finish at home to Real Sociedad on 28 January 2027 at 21:00 CET.

Serie A comes first. Juventus travel to Fiorentina for matchday 11 on Sunday 8 November, with kick-off at 20:45. AZ host Groningen in the Eredivisie on the same day.

#1501. Cardinale says MSE will give Milan ‘financial muscle’ and reiterates: “I will never sell”

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had launched the new holding company to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are big plans for the company.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Big 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

In an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding company?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ Currently, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term…

“Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how quickly…

“My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

“Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

“We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

“No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding company?

“I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be announced at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly quickly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management company.”

Does your plan include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the company I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the New York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading…

“Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”

In an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

“We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

“It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

“Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”

#1500. The unexpected email that led to Bukayo Saka's Socrates Award win at the Ballon d'Or: Inside Arsenal star's secret humanitarian work after his surprise win at London ceremony

Published: 08:07 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 08:13 EST, 11 November 2026

The sight of Bukayo Saka hobbling down the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or ceremony came as a surprise. Only those closest to him knew why he was there, and the years of toil that led to this moment.

While his England team-mate Harry Kane claimed the night's top on-pitch prize, Saka – who had suffered a thigh injury just days before against Kane's Bayern Munich – was at the London Palladium to collect the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

Joining a roll of honour that includes previous winners Vinicius Junior, Sadio Mane and Luis Enrique, Saka walked onto the stage, reached into his suit pocket and read a letter from a 14-year-old boy in Rwanda whose eyesight had been restored through his charity work.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal the scale of the Arsenal star's involvement over the last four years with the BigShoe charity, which funds operations, feeds children and helps with disaster relief across the world. From restoring the eyesight of that 14-year-old in Rwanda to helping provide life-saving procedures for 120 children in Nigeria, Saka's impact goes far beyond the stadiums he dazzles in.

And this is no passive act of philanthropy. BigShoe president Valerie Fiesser's phone is often inundated with messages from Saka when the charity is delivering projects in poverty-stricken countries such as Nigeria and Rwanda. Many of the project ideas come from the 25-year-old himself.

'Bukayo is really, really productive,' Fiesser tells Daily Mail Sport. 'He is really pushing how he wants to help. I think for him it is never fast enough to help. Sometimes Bukayo comes up with projects and he says, "Shouldn't we help here?" So he is really interested in it. It is not like he is just sending money and saying, "OK, nice, we'll do a project in Nigeria".

Bukayo Saka was handed the Ballon d'Or Socrates Award for his humanitarian work last month

Saka has worked with BigShoe charity for years - helping those in poverty-stricken countries

In 2023, Saka donated 50 containers to help provide shelter for 255 people impacted by the devastating earthquake in Morocco

'When we are on the ground, he is texting, "Is everything alright? Is everybody safe? Are all the children safe? Which services do we have? Can I see pictures? Send me pictures, send me pictures, send me pictures!"

BigShoe, a German-based charity founded during the 2006 World Cup, began years ago by funding life-changing surgery for Nourisson, a young girl from Togo born with a cleft lip and palate. The Togo national team, playing at their first World Cup, were based in the city of Wangen im Allgau, which brought the story to prominence in Germany.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 children around the globe having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food. The organisation has also worked with Antonio Rudiger, Paul Pogba and Saka's ex-Arsenal team-mates Mesut Ozil and Oleksandr Zinchenko.

Fiesser vividly remembers how Saka first got in touch, in early 2022.

'He just really randomly wrote us an email,' she says. 'He asked us if we can help together in Nigeria after seeing a project of another soccer player. He said, "I want to help children, I want to help people and can we do something". (It was) really just random.'

That initial conversation quickly developed into a project in late 2022 which funded 120 life-changing medical operations for children in Nigeria. Some of the youngsters were suffering from brain tumours, while others required treatment for hernias.

'This was an incredible project because it was the first project in Nigeria together with him,' she says. 'It was really life-changing for the children because some had a brain tumour, some had hernia problems.'

Saka has since helped support healthcare check-ups for more than 580 children in Rwanda and provide disaster relief after devastating earthquakes in Morocco and Turkey, while his involvement has extended far beyond financial backing.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 kids having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food

'We did a disaster relief where we provided homes for the earthquake victims in Morocco and Turkey and he was asking questions like, "Do they have electricity there?"' she says.

'He is really thinking, "Is it worth it, does it make sense to do this, or is it just putting the container and then the people do not have water and they cannot live there?" So he is really, really smart. And yes, I think he is an amazing human.

'It was never about him. It was always about the children and how we can help. It was never like, "OK, we are talking to one of the best players of the world." I think he is raised like this. His family made him the man he is now.

'I think he is raised like this, that you have to be a good human being and to help others and just have an impact in life.'

Saka and his family are directly involved in the projects, identifying communities in need and deciding exactly how support should be delivered. His mother, Adenike, is a key figure.

'We decide together where we can help, how we can help and then we actually help together,' Fiesser says. 'Me and his mother WhatsApp, call regularly. She has played a big part and is a driving force.

'Three months ago we renovated a school in Rwanda and we provided them with water filters for clean drinking water. We also built girls' changing rooms, a new soccer pitch and a new library. Bukayo's family was on the ground, twice.

'We decided after we saw that the families are really hungry in this area to do food packages. It is our next project in November and December.

'He (Saka) really wants to make a difference. He wants to change lives.'

While Saka will continue to chase trophies in Arsenal red and England white, his greatest legacy may ultimately be measured in the lives he has changed far beyond the football pitch.

#1499. McKennie fit for Fiorentina as Juventus chase a third straight win before the break

Weston McKennie is over the muscle problem that kept him out at AZ and is set to start in Florence on Sunday. A win would send Spalletti's depleted side into the international break on a three-match winning run.

Juventus close the round in Florence with a familiar midfielder back. Spalletti will hand Weston McKennie an immediate return to the side, Sky Sport Italia reports. The return comes at a useful moment for a squad that is still stretched.

#FiorentinaJuve 🔜 https://t.co/ST1eWZieA8

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 6, 2026

Celik and Conceição face late fitness checks and may only make the bench. Before the AZ match, Çelik was one of three Juventus players with at least two goals in this Europa League campaign, alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani. The club’s squad list had not yet been published.

Yildiz, Thuram, Locatelli, Grabara, Nico González and Ekhator are all unavailable. The expected shape is a 4-4-2. Vicario is in goal behind Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumí and Cabal. McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and Alajbegovic form the midfield, with Kolo Muani and Woltemade up front.

Spalletti will skip the usual pre-match press conference. The decision was put down only to the run of closely spaced fixtures.

History favours the visitors. Juventus have won 82 Serie A meetings with Fiorentina, the Viola have won 37, and 55 have been drawn. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against them, two fewer than Inter’s 277. A two-goal haul on Sunday would draw them level.

Kerim Alajbegovic has a milestone within reach. He can become the first foreign player in Juventus’s history to score in two top-flight games in a row before turning 20.

The stakes are clear. Victory would carry Juventus into the break with three wins in a row and strengthen their bid to rejoin the European race. After it, Juventus host Venezia on 22 November at 12:30, before a trip to Como on 29 November.

#1497. Spalletti skips Fiorentina preview as Juventus seek a first win over Vanoli

Luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina. Juventus arrive on two straight wins, chasing fourth place, against a coach Spalletti has never beaten.

Juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach. Sunday’s game at the Franchi kicks off at 20:45. The squad got back to Turin overnight from the Netherlands. The reason given is the club’s crowded run of fixtures, TuttoJuve reported. It is the last game before the international break.

The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November. Kerim Alajbegovic scored in the 70th minute. Aged 19 years and 41 days, no foreign player had ever found the net at a younger age in a Serie A game between Juventus and Napoli.

Four days later, Juventus won 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League. Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored. The result takes them to 10 points from four games in the competition. After the match, Spalletti described himself as very pleased with a solid team display against strong opponents. He felt his side should have added a third goal.

The league position still needs work. The club’s stated aim this season is fourth place, and Como currently hold that spot. The defence gives some grounds for confidence. Going back to last March, no side can match the Bianconeri’s tally of 12 shutouts. Roma are next on 11.

Vanoli and Spalletti have faced each other only twice as coaches. Both meetings were Fiorentina-Juventus fixtures last season. Last November they drew 1-1 at the Franchi. Filip Kostic gave Juventus the lead before Rolando Mandragora equalised with a long-range shot.

The hosts’ struggles on their own pitch offer Juventus an opening against a side yet to find its footing at home.

The fixture carries plenty of history. Sunday’s game is the 175th Serie A meeting between the sides, according to the club’s statistical preview. Juventus have won 82, Fiorentina 37, and 55 have ended level. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against Fiorentina. Two more would draw them level with Inter’s 277, the highest total by any side against the Viola.

Once the international break is over, Juventus’s next Serie A match is on 22 November.
