Tuchel will be delighted with the half-time score and England’s spirit after going behind so early. But how on earth have Spain only scored once? They’ve missed a couple of one-on-ones, hit the post and blazed over the bar. Highly entertaining and England will know they will have to defend better if they are going to hold on to their lead.

An absorbing and end-to-end first half is brought to an end. Somehow, despite the fact at one point they could have been 3-0 down, England lead 2-1 at the break.

Cucurella’s cross from the left loops all the way to the back post, where it strikes the frame of the goal. I do not think Cucurella meant that.

It is chances galore at both ends, with the latest falling to Ruiz, whose shot from the edge of the box is deflected wide for a corner. Bellingham heads away at the front post.

England gift the ball away so poorly and Yamal should punish them with his second goal of the game but he blazes high over the bar.

What on earth has happened to Spain? O’Reilly’s cross from the byline picks out Kane, who guides a header towards goal. Cucurella makes an absolute mess of things, effectively kneeing the ball past his keeper and into his own net. Kane will try and claim it but surely that has to go down as an own goal. 10 minutes ago, Spain should have been 3-0 up. Now, England are 2-1 ahead.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT

England are inches away from taking the lead. Saka drives forward towards the Spain box and lays it across to Kane, whose shot goes just wide. Should Kane have scored? Maybe.

SO CLOSE FROM KANE! 🫣England nearly go in front 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/YgoRblxuiH

Somehow, England are on level terms. Spain should have been 3-0 up but England equalise with a clinical counter-attack. Anderson wins the ball back for England on the edge of their own box and plays it forward to Gordon, who flicks it brilliantly first time into the path of Bellingham, who drives into the Spain half. Gordon is on his bike and is ready to receive the forward pass from Bellingham. Gordon takes it to the Spain box before slotting home clinically past Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd

England have missed Declan Rice’s delivery so far this evening. Saka has floated a couple of corners straight into the hands of Spain goalkeeper Simon and there have been some promising free-kicks wasted too.

No love lost between the Real Madrid team-mates Jude Bellingham and Marc Cucurella, there. Bellingham was unhappy with a challenge from the left-back and let’s just say they exchanged words afterwards.

If Olmo had slotted that home, the assist from Yamal would have been quite incredible. A quite sensational flick from Yamal plays Olmo in behind on the right side of the box and the latter’s shot goes narrowly wide of the far post.

Saka’s shot is blocked and the ball spins behind for an England corner out on the right. Saka takes the corner he won but his inswinger is caught by Unai Simon.

England want a penalty. Lewis-Skelly goes down inside the Spain penalty area under a challenge from Cubarsi and his appeals are waved away. The referee was spot on with that call.

That is a second sitter missed of the half from Torres and Spain should be 3-0 up. Rodri times his through ball to perfection and Torres’ first touch is glorious to take him past Anderson and away. Torres is one-on-one with Trafford and should score but his effort slides by the left post. How Spain are not 3-0 up is beyond me.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c

That is a waste from Bellingham. The Real Madrid man is found by Quansah on the edge of the box and Bellingham should get his shot off quickly but dithers for too long. Bellingham then goes down far too softly, wanting a free-kick, but those appeals are rightly waved away.

England have enjoyed more of the possession thus far but are still yet to register a shot through 25 minutes.

The Spain fans are certainly enjoying their night in north London. In general, they have a lot to be happy about currently holding the World Cup and Euros trophies as well as the fact that their team is 1-0 up this evening.

That is a big save from Trafford and a big miss from Torres. Yamal plays a through ball to pick out the run of Torres, whom many in the ground think is offside. However, he was clearly being played onside by Quansah and Torres, who is fine scoring form this season for PSG, should score with a one-on-one opportunity but is denied by Trafford. England could and perhaps should be 2-0 down.

Anderson plays a lovely switch from right to left to pick out Gordon in space. Gordon takes just one touch before getting it out of his feet quickly, curling a cross to the back post. He is looking for Saka but Cucurella just about deals with it, even though he did not know much about it. The ball appeared to come off Cucurella last but a goal-kick is given.

After a very shaky start, England are beginning to grow into the game, slowly, but it is gradually happening.

England are really not helping themselves at the moment, gifting the ball away in dangerous area. This time it is Lewis-Skelly who gives it away and Spain end up with a corner.

The delivery is drilled to the edge of the box, where Yamal’s powerful volley is blocked by Gordon.

Spain keep it alive and the ball comes back into the England box. Torres fires into the bottom corner but the offside flag goes up and replays show he was clearly offside.

The OFFSIDE Flag saves England's blushes 👀Ferran Torres saw his close range finish chalked off #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/unIj6NsO7z

England have their first sight of the Spain goal. Kane plays Gordon in down the left and the latter gets past his man easily. He gets to the byline before crossing but Unai Simon in the Spain goal is on hand to cut it out.

What on earth are you doing Guehi? Spain take the lead inside two minutes and it is a real gift. Guehi should pass to O’Reilly or Gordon to his left but instead comes back towards his own goal, seemingly unaware that Yamal is right behind him. What then follows is a clinical finish from Yamal, who drives into the England box before curling towards the far corner, with the ball going in off the inside of the post. We are under way at Wembley. There is VAR in use.

Tuchel was not shown on the big screens ahead of kick-off. He’s just got up off his seat for the first time and entered his technical area to complain about something.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”

In memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️Today's official matchday programme ⤵️

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

England’s plans for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel said. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

“For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”

Declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against New Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

#1411. Rio Ferdinand labels Man United's Michael Carrick sacking 'like ChatGPT' - with 142-word statement sent by communications department and no message from club chiefs

Published: 07:20 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:22 EST, 12 November 2026

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand has called for 'a face' to explain the decision to sack Michael Carrick after comparing the club's statement announcing his dismissal to ChatGPT.

Carrick's dismissal was confirmed in a 142-word statement released at 10.37am, which was sent out by Man United's communications department.

Man United have moved closer to appointing former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Man United's key decision makers, including chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, have not issued a message following the decision to part ways with Carrick.

Ferdinand, who played alongside Carrick at Man United, has called for officials to front up to the decision in a post on social media.

'Man United statement like Chat GPT… I wanna hear a voice!' Ferdinand wrote. 'I want to see a face to this…'

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season

Man United's leadership, including minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, were not named in the club's statement

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand called for 'a face' to speak about the decision after comparing the club's statement to ChatGPT

Man United's club statement confirming the decision read: 'Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

'Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

'The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.'

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, Berrada and Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager

Ferdinand, speaking on Rio Presents, claimed Carrick had been disrespected in the way his dismissal had been handled.

'You do everything you can to make this end in the most amicable and respectful and pleasant way possible,' Ferdinand said.

'I think the way it has been done, it could have been done better. I think the leaks coming out of the club are terrible, they don't reflect well on anybody at all.

'It adds to the disrespect to the person in charge at the time. It is terrible to play out in the public like this. The minimum you should get is a bit of respect.'

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins – 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager – six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

#1410. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

Jordan Pickford did the same at the Azteca before England’s win against Mexico in the summer. England players were split for the final part of the warm-up, with defenders doing drills as a unit, while midfielders and attackers did shooting.

Yes, for sure [this is as good as I’ve felt in an England shirt. My football IQ, I’m getting better and better, smarter and smarter. I need time to really feel at home, to feel comfortable and once I have that I don’t look back.

I knew exactly where I wanted to go, where I needed to go but I needed some guidance. I think the same way as him [Jude]. We don’t think there’s any limit on what we can achieve, wanting to win, wanting to win in a good way by going for the throat. Fearlessness.

It ate me up for a good couple of weeks after [losing the semi-final]. I’d scored… on the same pitch as Messi, the man I idolised as a kid. It was the highest possible moment of my entire life. And within 20 minutes it had come completely crashing down. There’s been a lot of controversy, a lot of talk about that. Going forward, if we are going to lose a game, it’s going to be like how we lost to Spain. We went for their throats, we missed a penalty and lost the game. But the way we went for them, no regrets. I want to stay as far away from that [regret] as possible.

[Did you ever think you would sign for Barcelona?] Yes. No one ever achieves anything in life by playing it safe. My personality is based on being bold, taking risks and going for whatever you want.

At this level we’re all as talented as each other but only the most mentally competitive and driven people can maintain success for a long time.

I always thought in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never respected my quality and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick. In Barcelona if you’re not technical, if you’re not smart, you’d stand out like a sore thumb.

[Where do you see this squad in two years?] European champions.

The intensity we played with and the way we took it to the best team in the world [is what we’ve taken out of the Spain game]. We can be really proud of that. It was really good. Obviously tight margins decide games but overall we’re happy with the way we dusted the World Cup off and all that emotion.

Massively [relishing a run in the No 10 position in place of Bellingham]. I want to try and show what I can do in that role and make a positive impact.

The atmosphere here [is always intense] and they have a new coach. We’ve done our research. We have to respect them. It’s going to be difficult and it’s up to us to hold our nerve.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, said the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”

Trevoh Chalobah will earn his third England cap in tonight’s Nations League match against Czech Republic. The Como centre-back, 27, played in the 6-4 defeat of France in the Bronze final at the World Cup and his other appearance for the Three Lions was in the defeat by Senegal last year.

Trent Alexander-Arnold will make his first England appearance in 15 months after being given a start. The Real Madrid full-back, who was not selected for the World Cup in the summer, earned his last cap against Andorra in 2025.

He replaces Jarell Quansah in Thomas Tuchel’s line-up that lost to Spain at the weekend.

“Trent had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us,” said Tuchel on the eve of the game at Fortuna Arena.

“We’re good. Everything is fine. He’s ready to go. He has qualities that you all know, like he’s strong on the ball, excellent crossing, good finishing. And very, very good on the ball. That’s basically what he brings.”

Ezri Konsa, who missed team training on the day before this game, is out. Morgan Rogers, meanwhile, steps in for Jude Bellingham in the No10 role as Tuchel looks to juggle four matches in 11 days during this extended international break.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line to make his first England start under head coach Thomas Tuchel for tonight’s Nations League game against Czech Republic.

Injuries to Nico O’Reilly and Ezri Konsa have forced Tuchel into changes at the back, with Alexander-Arnold expected to come in at right-back, Trevoh Chalobah to replace Konsa and Lewis Hall to step in for O’Reilly.

Alexander-Arnold has made only one appearance under Tuchel, as a substitute in a World Cup qualifying win against Andorra in June 2025. His last start for England came under interim head coach Lee Carsley, when he scored in a victory over Finland.

Jude Belllingham could be given a rest after playing the full 90 minutes in the defeat by Spain, which would give Morgan Rogers an opportunity in the No 10 position.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

#1409. Michael Carrick is SACKED by Man United: Manager leaves training ground just 2½ hours after arriving - and now Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over

Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026

Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.

Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

In a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick have indicated. They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season

Carrick was seen leaving the training ground less than two and a half hours later

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's new manager

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday morning after it had emerged that Berrada and Wilcox were heading to Monaco to recommend his sacking and did so again on Wednesday when it transpired United were closing in on an agreement to bring in Pochettino as his successor.

The current United States national team manager reached a verbal agreement with Man United to take over on Wednesday. United then made a formal approach to US Soccer shortly after, with the club having to trigger the 54-year-old Argentine's £7million release clause.

The final nail in Carrick’s coffin came in Sunday's dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which saw United stuck in the relegation zone in 18th position.

The handling of Carrick’s departure has been particularly damning on Ineos and the shot-callers at United, not least given he was given no show of public support when he continued in post following an emergency board meeting after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

A defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez badly let his manager down by getting sent off, and a win over Roma to go with the draw against Villa, was not enough of a sign that it will turn around for the board to keep faith.

With Carrick's departure, it pushes the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million. Buying Pochettino out of his contract with the US national team will cost another £7m. Adding his large coaching staff will take millions more.

Matchgoing supporters will be sad to see Carrick go and made those feelings clear in recent games when he was loudly cheered at the end of matches, with the ire and frustration levelled against players and executives.

Optimism heading into the campaign was sky high given that no team in the Premier League performed better than Carrick's side between January and May.

But that level of success and dominance has long since evaporated after a shambolic start to the current campaign - and it has cost the 45-year-old his job just five months after the ink dried on a new deal.

It has been a season in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league all season.

A season in which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned his manager's tactics and Martinez eviscerated the hierarchy for hanging Carrick and the players out to dry. Fernandes was even dropped for the first time in five years for the Bournemouth humiliation.

Questions will continue to be asked of those upstairs, with Berrada and Wilcox now on to their third permanent manager this year alone and their fourth in their tenure having burned through Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick since taking control of football operations in February 2024.

It means Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (pictured on Thursday morning) need a third manager this year as INEOS' running of the football club comes under scrutiny once more

Sunday's draw with Aston Villa proved to be the final nail in the coffin for the United boss

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players

Amorim lasted 14 months in the role, even in spite of embarrassing defeats to the likes of League Two Grimsby Town, but for Carrick it was a dream job that would run until early November and end in him being unceremoniously dumped at the training ground by Wilcox.

Carrick vowed after the Villa draw that he wouldn’t walk away and took on a spiky side when quizzed on his future by reporters. After a week of shame against the board, he has finally been put out of his misery.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins - 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager - six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Now it looks set to be Pochettino’s challenge to turn this massively underperforming squad around, something former United star Gary Neville believes is a mightily difficult task given the 'unprofessional' squad the new man will inherit.

'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned [Carrick] for a few months. They have, they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast recently.

'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though.

'He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.

'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

#1408. Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer1, in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)2. Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

Aberrant enhancer-driven transcription sustains many cancers, including metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)3,4. AR, a central driver of mCRPC, undergoes ligand-induced activation and dimerization upon binding to androgen response element (ARE)-enriched enhancers and assembling cancer-specific neo-enhanceosomes4,5,6. These complexes depend on the paralogous acetyltransferases p300 and CBP7. p300 has been identified as the predominant paralogue supporting AR-positive (AR+) prostate cancer growth, and the p300/CBP-dependent enhancer mark H2B N-terminal acetylation (H2BNTac) and AR–p300 co-bound enhancer activity are increased in prostate tumours8. Previous studies showed that the N-terminal domain (NTD) of AR interacts with p3002, and this interaction stimulates the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity of p300, leading to enhancer remodelling and transcriptional activation by establishing a permissive chromatin environment9,10. Although p300/CBP-targeted therapies have been developed for castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)11,12, global p300/CBP inhibition may cause toxicity in normal tissues13.

Chemically induced proximity (CIP) reprograms protein–protein interactions to manipulate cellular functions14,15. Established CIP modalities include proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), which promote target protein degradation via E3 ligase recruitment16; regulated induced proximity targeting chimeras (RIPTACs), which couple disease-associated proteins to essential effectors17,18; transcriptional/epigenetic chemical inducers of proximity (TCIPs), which redirect transcriptional coactivators19,20,21; and targeted relocalization activating molecules (TRAMs), which alter protein localization22. These approaches predominantly connect non-native partners. Here we introduce DALTACs, which enforce neomorphic domain interactions between physiological partners to disable endogenous oncogenic complexes. DALTAC-1 (JZY3032) connects the ligand-binding domain (LBD) of AR to the bromodomain (BRD) of p300/CBP, reprogramming substrate engagement, eliminating H2BNTac and suppressing AR–p300/CBP-dependent transcription. DALTAC-1 outperforms combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition, selectively targets AR-dependent prostate cancer, and induces tumour regression without overt toxicity, establishing domain-level rewiring as a promising therapeutic strategy.

Previous studies established that AR physically interacts with the coactivator p300 through its NTD2, and that dimerized transcription factors can stimulate p300 HAT activity9. To reprogram this native interaction, we designed heterobifunctional molecules that tether an AR-LBD binder to a p300/CBP-BRD binder through an appropriate linker. We reasoned that these molecules would induce non-native AR–p300/CBP interactions and thereby inhibit the growth of AR+ cancer cells by concurrently inhibiting both AR and p300/CBP functions (Fig. 1a).

a, Schematic showing how DALTAC-1 rewires domain–domain interactions of the native AR–p300/CBP complex. Created in BioRender; Young, E. https://BioRender.com/ehpy9qp (2026). b, Structure of DALTAC-1 (JZY3032), comprising AR and p300/CBP binders connected by a linker. c, Cellular thermal shift assay of VCaP cells treated with DMSO or DALTAC-1 (100 nM, 4 h). Left, immunoblots showing stabilization of p300, CBP and AR, but not BRD4. Right, protein levels normalized to the lowest temperature condition (three independent experiments). d, Dose–response curves and IC50 values of AR+ VCaP and LNCaP cells treated with DALTAC-1, CBPD-409 or p300/CBPi plus ARi for five days. Data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 replicated wells; three independent experiments. e, Ranked IC50 values for DALTAC-1 and CBPD-409 across different human cell lines after five-day treatments. Colours indicate specific cell types. PCa, prostate cancer.

To test this premise, we designed and synthesized a series of heterobifunctional molecules using a potent p300/CBP-BRD inhibitor (GNE-04912) and a selective AR-LBD binder23 tethered through a linker (Extended Data Fig. 1a). We selected the tethering site in the p300/CBP-BRD inhibitor based upon the co-crystal structure with GNE-049 and its analogues, which showed that our selected tethering site was exposed to the solvent environment24. Similarly, we chose the tethering site in the AR binder on the basis of our modelled complex structure with AR and extensive structure–activity relationships reported for this class of AR inhibitors23,25. We evaluated our synthesized compounds with proliferation assays in AR+ LNCaP and 22Rv1 cells, which were shown to be responsive to p300/CBP-BRD inhibitors and PROTAC degraders11,26. GNE-049, the AR binder JZY3221, and their combination were included as controls. Treatment with GNE-049, JZY3221 or their combination showed limited inhibitory activity, particularly in 22Rv1 cells (Extended Data Fig. 1b).

To optimize these heterobifunctional molecules, we replaced the tetrahydropyran group of GNE-049 with a piperidinyl group that preserves p300 binding24 and systematically varied linker composition, length and rigidity (Extended Data Fig. 1b and Supplementary Note 1). Several compounds showed substantially greater anti-proliferative activity than the parent-inhibitor combination. Compound 7 (JZY3031) emerged as a lead, with half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 1.9 nM and 2.6 nM in LNCaP and 22Rv1 cells, respectively, and was more potent than the inhibitor combination (Extended Data Fig. 1b).

Replacing an oxygen atom in the AR-binding moiety of compound 7 with an N-methyl group, a modification previously shown to improve oral bioavailability25, generated JZY3032 (Fig. 1b). JZY3032 achieved IC50 values of 0.26 nM and 1.0 nM in LNCaP and 22Rv1 cells, respectively, and was more potent than the parent-inhibitor combination (Extended Data Fig. 1b). JZY3032 also showed improved systemic exposure and 18.5% oral bioavailability in mice, despite its high molecular mass of 975 Da (Extended Data Fig. 1c).

In an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) measuring induced AR–p300 complex formation, compound 7 and JZY3032 were the most potent and effective compounds that we tested. JZY3032 also produced the strongest inhibition of AR transcriptional activity in HEK293 ARE–GFP reporter cells (Extended Data Fig. 1b). By contrast, three enzalutamide-based bifunctional molecules were substantially less active in VCaP, LNCaP and 22Rv1 cells, demonstrating the importance of the AR-binding moiety (Extended Data Fig. 1d,e).

Based on its cellular, biochemical and pharmacokinetic properties, we designated JZY3032 as DALTAC-1. We also generated Neg-1, with reduced p300/CBP binding24, and Neg-2, with reduced AR binding27 (Extended Data Fig. 1f). Fluorescence polarization assays confirmed their intended binding profiles (Extended Data Fig. 1g–i). Cellular thermal shift assays further showed that DALTAC-1 stabilized AR, p300 and CBP, but not BRD4, supporting selective engagement of its intended targets (Fig. 1c and Extended Data Fig. 1j).

To assess the activity and selectivity of DALTAC-1, we compared its anti-proliferative activity with the p300/CBP dual degrader CBPD-4098 and the combined treatment with the p300/CBP-BRD inhibitor GNE-049 (p300/CBPi) and AR-LBD binder JZY3221 (ARi). DALTAC-1 potently inhibited growth across all tested AR+ prostate cancer cell lines, with activity comparable or superior to CBPD-409 and consistently greater than p300/CBPi plus ARi in CellTiter-Glo (CTG) and colony-formation assays (Fig. 1d and Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). This superiority suggests a gain-of-function mechanism arising from enforced miswiring of AR–p300 domain interactions. DALTAC-1 also retained potent activity in the AR-V7-high, p300/CBP-dependent 22Rv1 and CWR-R1 models (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b) and outperformed enzalutamide, darolutamide28,29, the AR PROTAC degrader ARV-76630 and the recently reported AR–BRD4 RIPTAC-131 (Extended Data Fig. 2c). By contrast, the inactive analogues Neg-1 and Neg-2 showed substantially reduced activity, and excess p300/CBPi or ARi competitively attenuated DALTAC-1 activity, demonstrating that engagement of both targets is required (Extended Data Fig. 2d,e).

Compared with CBPD-409, DALTAC-1 exhibited markedly reduced cytotoxicity in AR-negative yet p300-dependent Kelly and NCI-H211 cells8 (Extended Data Fig. 2f). It remained highly active in AR+ MDA-MB-453 cells32, which depend on both AR and p300/CBP, but showed minimal activity in AR+ U-87 MG cells33, which were less sensitive to CBPD-409 and ARV-766 (Extended Data Fig. 2g). Across a broader cancer cell line panel, CBPD-409 displayed activity across multiple lineages, whereas DALTAC-1 selectively inhibited AR+ prostate cancer cells (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Fig. 2h). Moreover, a 4-h DALTAC-1 pulse followed by washout produced inhibition comparable to continuous exposure, whereas CBPD-409 or p300/CBPi plus ARi activity was substantially diminished after washout (Extended Data Fig. 2i,j). Collectively, these findings establish DALTAC-1 as a potent, durable and lineage-selective heterobifunctional compound whose activity depends on dual AR and p300/CBP engagement.

Ternary complex formation is central to the CIP strategy34. Using purified proteins, DALTAC-1 induced AR–p300 association in a concentration-dependent manner, whereas the combined AR and p300/CBP inhibitors and the binding-deficient analogues Neg-1 and Neg-2 did not induce association (Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 3a). Biolayer interferometry (BLI) further demonstrated DALTAC-1-dependent complex formation. In the presence of 10 μM DALTAC-1, titration of GST–AR-LBD produced concentration-dependent binding to p300, with an apparent dissociation constant (Kd) of 333.1 nM, whereas minimal interaction between GST–AR-LBD and p300 was detected under the DMSO control condition (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 3b). Reciprocally, titration of DALTAC-1 at a fixed GST–AR-LBD concentration (1 μM) progressively increased the binding response, yielding an apparent Kd of approximately 4.3 μM (Extended Data Fig. 3c). Neither DALTAC-1, GST–AR-LBD, nor their combination produced significant binding to immobilized Flag–FOXA1 (residues 1–268), excluding nonspecific association with the immobilized protein or sensor (Extended Data Fig. 3d). Moreover, the individual AR-LBD and p300/CBP-BRD inhibitors, alone or combined, did not induce complex formation, whereas excess p300/CBP-BRD inhibitor markedly attenuated the DALTAC-1-induced BLI signal (Extended Data Fig. 3e,f). Together, these results demonstrate that DALTAC-1 specifically recruits the AR-LBD to p300 to promote concentration-dependent formation of the AR-LBD–DALTAC-1–p300 ternary complex.

a, Immunoblot analysis showing that DALTAC-1 induced a dose-dependent interaction between purified full-length AR and p300 proteins. Purified p300 (0.2 or 1 μg) was incubated with or without purified HA–AR (1 μg) and the indicated concentrations of DALTAC-1, followed by immunoprecipitation (IP) with anti-HA (three independent experiments). b, Representative fitted BLI sensorgrams showing concentration-dependent binding of titrated GST–AR-LBD to immobilized Flag–p300 in the presence of 10 μM DALTAC-1, with an apparent Kd of 333.1 nM (three independent experiments). c, The top 30 proteins whose interactions with p300 were significantly (P < 0.05) increased in DALTAC-1-treated VCaP cells, as determined by immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry analysis. AR is shown in red. n = 3 independently treated and processed VCaP cell samples per treatment condition. Two-sided moderated t-test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. d, Immunoblot analysis of indicated proteins and histone marks in VCaP cells treated with 100 nM of indicated compounds for noted durations (three independent experiments). Vinculin is used as same-gel p300 loading control; H2B is a separate-gel control from the same samples. e, Volcano plot showing altered lysine acetylation levels in VCaP cells treated with 100 nM DALTAC-1 versus DMSO for 12 h. H2BNTac sites are highlighted in blue and components of the AR complex are highlighted in red. Data are plotted from n = 3 independently treated and processed samples. Statistical significance was assessed using two-sided unpaired t-tests followed by Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. FC, fold change. f, RNA-seq heat maps for AR and p300/CBP target genes in VCaP cells treated with DALTAC-1 or p300/CBPi plus ARi (100 nM, 4 h). n = 2 independently treated and processed samples. g, Immunoblot analysis of indicated proteins in VCaP cells treated with 100 nM indicated compounds for 4 and 24 h. H2B is a separate-gel control from the same samples (three independent experiments).

Intracellular ternary complex formation was confirmed by ELISA, which showed that DALTAC-1, but not Neg-1 or Neg-2, enhanced AR–p300 association in VCaP cells (Extended Data Fig. 3g). Co-immunoprecipitation similarly demonstrated that DALTAC-1 enhanced the interaction between AR and p300/CBP (Extended Data Fig. 3h,i). Consistently, reciprocal immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry analyses identified AR as strongly enriched in p300 immunoprecipitates, and p300/CBP were among the most enriched AR-associated proteins following DALTAC-1 treatment (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 3j,k). Proximity ligation assays (PLAs) further showed DALTAC-1 increased AR–p300 proximity, which was competitively blocked by either p300/CBPi or ARi (Extended Data Fig. 3l,m). Sequential co-immunoprecipitation of co-expressed Flag–AR, haemagglutinin (HA)–AR, and V5-p300 showed that DALTAC-1 maintained the interaction of HA–AR with Flag–AR from p300-containing complexes, indicating the incorporation of multiple AR molecules into the DALTAC-1-induced complex and supporting AR dimerization within the complex (Extended Data Fig. 3n). In 22Rv1 cells, DALTAC-1 enhanced p300 association with full-length AR but not the LBD-deficient AR-V7 variant, demonstrating the LBD dependence of the association (Extended Data Fig. 3o). DALTAC-1 also promoted p300 association with the DNA-binding-deficient AR-C619Y mutant35 (Extended Data Fig. 3p), indicating that complex formation does not require AR binding to DNA. Together, these findings demonstrate that DALTAC-1 induces the formation of a LBD-dependent AR–p300 complex.

Domain-resolved interaction mapping in HEK293 cells showed minimal basal association between AR and the p300 core region, comprising the BRD, RING/PHD and HAT domains, yet DALTAC-1 strongly enhanced this interaction (Extended Data Fig. 3q). Reciprocal domain mapping demonstrated that DALTAC-1 selectively recruited the AR-LBD, but not the AR-NTD, to p300 (Extended Data Fig. 3r). Accordingly, co-expressed AR-LBD and p300 core region showed minimal basal association but robust complex formation following DALTAC-1 treatment (Extended Data Fig. 3s), establishing a non-native AR-LBD–p300 core interaction.

To investigate its structural basis, we modelled the AR-LBD–DALTAC-1–p300-BRD ternary complex and the corresponding binary complexes, followed by 1-µs molecular dynamics simulations. The top-scoring ternary model predicted an AR–p300 interface stabilized by polar and hydrophobic interactions (Extended Data Fig. 3t). Key contacts included salt bridges between Asp1088 of p300 and Arg871 of AR and between Arg1133 of p300 and Glu872 of AR; hydrogen bonds involving AR Arg871–p300 Gly1085 and AR Ile816–p300 Leu1083; hydrophobic packing between Ile816 of AR and Leu1083 of p300; and a cation–π interaction between His874 of AR and the piperazine moiety of DALTAC-1. Molecular mechanics-generalized born surface area (MM-GBSA) analysis yielded a more favourable model-dependent interaction-energy estimate for the ternary complex (−161.8 ± 0.6 kcal mol−1) than for the DALTAC-1–AR (−81.4 ± 0.6 kcal mol−1) or DALTAC-1–p300 (−90.3 ± 0.4 kcal mol−1) binary complexes (Extended Data Fig. 3u,v). Computational removal of DALTAC−1 yielded an AR–p300 interface energy of −53.5 ± 1.1 kcal mol−1, consistent with favourable protein complementarity (Extended Data Fig. 3v).

Experimentally, mutation of the predicted interface residues in AR(R871A/E872A) and p300(D1088A/R1133A) substantially impaired DALTAC-1-induced complex formation (Extended Data Fig. 3w). Together, these findings establish that DALTAC-1 rewires AR–p300 domain interactions to form a stable ternary complex, providing a mechanistic basis for its downstream epigenetic and transcriptional effects.

In contrast to the p300/CBP degrader CBPD-409, DALTAC-1 did not reduce p300/CBP protein abundance but rapidly suppressed H3K27ac and H2BK20ac, two histone marks associated with active enhancers (Fig. 2d and Extended Data Fig. 4a–c). H2BNTac is deposited exclusively by p300/CBP and marks active enhancers in prostate cancer8. Our data demonstrate that DALTAC-1 exerts a de novo heterobifunctional effect by potently suppressing this critical histone mark without degrading p300/CBP. This level of H2BNTac suppression was not observed with the inactive analogues Neg-1 and Neg-2 or with the combination of AR and p300/CBP inhibitors (Extended Data Fig. 4a–c). DALTAC-1 also showed limited activity in AR-negative Kelly cells, supporting its AR-dependent selectivity (Extended Data Fig. 4d). Furthermore, in HEK293 cells, DALTAC-1-driven loss of H2BNTac increased in direct proportion to the amount of ectopically expressed AR, underscoring that both AR and p300 are required for DALTAC activity (Extended Data Fig. 4e). Moreover, a 2-h DALTAC-1 pulse caused sustained suppression of histone acetylation and MYC expression after washout, whereas the effects of combined AR and p300/CBP inhibitors were markedly reduced (Extended Data Fig. 4f).

Beyond histone substrates, p300/CBP acetylate non-histone regulators of transcription and signal transduction36. Whereas p300/CBP HAT inhibitors and degraders broadly suppress histone and non-histone acetylation7,8, acetyl-lysine profiling in VCaP cells revealed a distinct acetylation signature induced by DALTAC-1. DALTAC-1 strongly suppressed global histone acetylation, particularly enhancer-associated H2BNTac, more potently than combined p300/CBP and AR inhibition (Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 4g–i). Consistently, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry identified H2B as the most significantly displaced p300 interactor, indicating disruption of p300 engagement with its canonical histone substrate (Extended Data Fig. 3j).

Concurrently, DALTAC-1, but not combined p300/CBP and AR inhibition, increased acetylation of AR and its cofactors SRC2 and SRC337 (Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 4g,h,j,k). AR acetylation occurred in the NTD, suggesting that DALTAC-1-induced ternary complex formation redirects p300 catalytic activity towards the N terminus of AR as well as its associated cofactors. In an ARE reporter assay, glutamine substitution of the five SRC2 lysines most strongly acetylated by DALTAC-1 (multi-K-Q) modestly increased AR activity relative to wild-type SRC2, whereas alanine substitution (multi-K-A) modestly reduced it, indicating that acetylation at these sites has limited effects on SRC2 coactivator function (Extended Data Fig. 4l,m). Thus, DALTAC-1 suppresses enhancer-linked histone acetylation while selectively increasing acetylation of AR and its associated cofactors.

We next examined how DALTAC-1-mediated reprogramming of p300 substrate engagement affects transcription. DALTAC-1 strongly suppressed AR activity in an ARE–GFP reporter assay and repressed canonical AR target genes, whereas Neg-1, Neg-2 or combined p300/CBP and AR inhibition exhibited weaker effects (Extended Data Fig. 5a–c). RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) in VCaP cells revealed downregulation of androgen response, p300/CBP target, MYC target and MTORC1 signalling pathways (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 5d–f). Chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing (ChIP–seq) further showed rapid RNA polymerase II (Pol II) displacement from AR and p300 target loci (Extended Data Fig. 5g). Together, unlike the transcriptional activation mechanism of TCIPs19,20, DALTAC-1 represses AR–p300/CBP-driven oncogenic transcription.

Consistently, DALTAC-1 and the p300/CBP degrader CBPD-409 markedly reduced prostate-specific antigen (PSA), CCND1 and NKX3-1 protein levels, whereas combined p300/CBP and AR inhibition had modest effects on these proteins (Fig. 2g). Quantitative proteomics confirmed selective depletion of AR- and MYC-regulated proteins without reducing AR or p300/CBP abundance (Extended Data Fig. 5h). Together, these results show that DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate utilization to broadly suppress AR-driven oncogenic transcription.

We next tested whether this activity requires an antagonist-derived AR binder. We replaced the AR moiety of DALTAC-1 with enobosarm38, a non-steroidal AR agonist, to generate JZY4055 (Extended Data Fig. 5i). JZY4055 potently inhibited growth of AR+ VCaP cells (Extended Data Fig. 5j). Whereas enobosarm activated canonical AR target genes, JZY4055 repressed these genes and reduced p300/CBP-dependent H2BK20ac and H3K27ac, as well as the expression of AR- and p300/CBP-regulated proteins NKX3-1 and MYC (Extended Data Fig. 5k,l). These data demonstrate that AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-mediated transcriptional repression does not require an antagonist-derived AR binder.

p300/CBP are central AR coactivators that sustain oncogenic transcription through enhancer-associated histone acetylation8. To investigate how DALTAC-1 modulates p300 chromatin occupancy, we performed p300 ChIP–seq in VCaP cells. DALTAC-1 markedly expanded and redistributed p300 binding genome-wide (Fig. 3a). Approximately 40% of DALTAC-1-depleted peaks were promoter-proximal, whereas gained peaks occurred predominantly in intronic and distal intergenic regions, with only approximately 10% being located near promoters, indicating increased enhancer engagement (Fig. 3b). At AR-binding enhancer sites identified under DMSO (control) conditions, DALTAC-1 proportionally increased AR and p300/CBP occupancy (Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 6a,b). Motif analysis revealed that gained p300 and CBP peaks were strongly enriched for canonical palindromic AREs and closely related nuclear receptor motifs, including progesterone- and glucocorticoid-response elements (PRE and GRE)39 (Fig. 3d and Extended Data Fig. 6c,d). These findings demonstrate that DALTAC-1 redistributes p300/CBP through AR-dependent recruitment and stabilizes neomorphic AR–p300/CBP complexes on enhancer chromatin.

UTR, untranslated region. c, ChIP–seq read-density heat maps of AR and p300 at AR-bound enhancer sites in VCaP cells treated with DMSO or 100 nM DALTAC-1 for 3 h (n = 1). d, HOMER analysis showing the fold enrichment and statistical significance of sequence motifs at non-promoter p300-binding sites in VCaP cells treated with DMSO or 100 nM DALTAC-1 for 3 h. DALTAC-1 also significantly reshaped the AR cistrome (Fig. 3e). DALTAC-1 treatment increased AR occupancy at palindromic AREs while reducing binding at FOXA1–AR chimeric motifs associated with oncogenic AR neo-enhanceosomes40 (Fig. 3e,f and Extended Data Fig. 6e–g). Thus, rather than uniformly increasing AR binding, DALTAC-1 redirected AR away from oncogenic enhancers and concentrated it at canonical nuclear receptor response elements. Because AREs share substantial sequence similarity with PREs39, we examined whether their enrichment reflected progesterone receptor (PR) activation. DALTAC-1 instead reduced PR occupancy genome-wide while increasing AR occupancy at PR-binding sites (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i), indicating that these shared motifs were predominantly engaged by AR. Despite increased AR and p300/CBP binding, DALTAC-1 markedly decreased coactivator (BRD4 and ERG) recruitment, Pol II loading, and histone acetylation (H3K27ac and H2BK20ac) at AR/p300 co-bound enhancers (Extended Data Fig. 6j,k). DALTAC-1 therefore stabilized AR–p300/CBP chromatin binding while functionally decommissioning the associated transcriptional complexes.

Oncogenic transcription factors such as ERG and FOXA1 mutants are known to redirect AR to non-canonical AREs, thereby forming cancer-specific AR neo-enhanceosomes that drive lineage-dependent oncogene programs8,41. In TMPRSS2–ERG fusion-positive VCaP cells42, DALTAC-1 globally reduced ERG occupancy, although a subset of new ERG peaks emerged in intronic and distal intergenic regions (Extended Data Fig. 7a–d). Motif analysis revealed that DALTAC-1 depleted ERG binding at canonical ETS motifs and redistributed ERG towards palindromic AREs (Extended Data Fig. 7e). At non-promoter AR–ERG co-bound regions, DALTAC-1 increased AR and p300 occupancy, modestly increased SRC2 binding, and minimally altered FOXA1 occupancy (Extended Data Fig. 7f–h). Nonetheless, ERG and BRD4 binding declined, whereas Pol II occupancy and enhancer-associated histone acetylation were almost completely lost (Extended Data Fig. 7i). Thus, DALTAC-1 collapses AR–ERG neo-enhancers into a transcriptionally inactive state despite increased AR–p300 occupancy, dismantling the oncogenic output of the AR–ERG neo-enhanceosome (Fig. 3g and Extended Data Fig. 7j).

To assess DALTAC-1 efficacy across prostate cancer subtypes, we tested organoids derived from genetically engineered mouse models. We treated organoids derived from wild-type, Rosa26ERG/Pten−/−, Pten−/−, FOXA1 R265–71del+/+/Trp53−/− and Trp53−/− mouse prostates with DALTAC-141,43. DALTAC-1 preferentially reduced the number and size of Rosa26ERG/Pten−/− and FOXA1 R265–71del+/+/Trp53−/− organoids and suppressed MYC and CCND1 relative to wild-type, Pten−/− and Trp53−/− organoids (Extended Data Fig. 8a–d). Given that ERG and mutant FOXA1 enhance AR activity and sustain the AR neo-enhanceosome5,41,43,44, these findings suggest that DALTAC-1 effectively suppresses AR-driven prostate cancer. Furthermore, we evaluated DALTAC-1 efficacy across organoids derived from patient-derived xenograft (PDX) tumours45,46. Consistently, DALTAC-1 potently inhibited AR+ organoids, particularly AR+/ERG+ models (Fig. 4a). Thus, DALTAC-1 exhibits potent, lineage-selective activity across mouse and human organoid models.

To evaluate in vivo activity of DALTAC-1, we first examined VCaP castration-resistant prostate cancer (VCaP-CRPC) xenografts established in castrated male severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) mice (Extended Data Fig. 9a). Mice were randomized to DALTAC-1 administered intraperitoneally (30 mg kg−1) or orally (60 mg kg−1), or an equipotent combination of p300/CBPi and ARi. Intraperitoneal DALTAC-1 induced tumour regression in 75% (12 out of 16) of tumours, whereas oral dosing also robustly suppressed tumour growth and outperformed the combined inhibitors (Fig. 4b and Extended Data Fig. 9b–d). In vivo PLA confirmed increased AR–p300 proximity in treated tumours (Fig. 4c). COMET multiplex immunofluorescence (COMET-mIF) analyses revealed that DALTAC-1 reduced ERG, PSA, MYC, Ki-67, H3K27ac and H2BK20ac without decreasing AR, p300 or CBP abundance, consistent with non-degradative AR–p300/CBP rewiring (Fig. 4d and Extended Data Fig. 9e,f).

We next assessed the efficacy of DALTAC-1 in two prostate cancer PDX models, MDA-PCa-146-12 and MDA-PCa-18345,47. DALTAC-1 significantly inhibited MDA-PCa-146-12 growth (Extended Data Fig. 9g) and induced rapid, sustained regression of TMPRSS2–ERG-positive, PTEN-deficient MDA-PCa-183 tumours, with no progression observed during the 35-day treatment period (Extended Data Fig. 9h–k). In the MDA-PCa-183 model, DALTAC-1 induced marked tumour regression throughout the 50-day treatment period, whereas enzalutamide produced only modest tumour growth inhibition and ARV-766 was less effective than DALTAC-1 (Fig. 4e,f). Following treatment withdrawal, DALTAC-1-treated tumours showed no evident recurrence for 16 days, whereas ARV-766-treated tumours regrew (Fig. 4e,f). DALTAC-1 was well tolerated, with no significant changes in body weight, liver or kidney function, or haematological parameters (Extended Data Fig. 10a–e). Together, DALTAC-1 produces potent and durable antitumour responses across prostate cancer models through selective, non-degradative reprogramming of AR–p300/CBP complexes.

Recent advances in CIP have led to the development of a diverse array of compounds capable of modulating protein functions through enforced protein–protein interactions14. RIPTACs induce proximity between a target protein and a pan-essential effector that disrupts the function of the essential effector, leading to selective cancer cell death while sparing healthy cells17. By contrast, TCIPs recruit transcriptional coactivators to specific genomic loci, paradoxically activating the target pathway by enhancing transcription of pro-apoptotic genes that are normally repressed by corepressors such as BCL619,20. The emerging clinical activity of daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), which forms a ternary complex with cyclophilin A and active RAS, further supports the translational potential of proximity-induced pharmacology48. Recent molecular glue degraders further demonstrate that small molecules can stabilize pre-existing or newly enabled protein interfaces and alter target organization to promote E3 ligase-dependent degradation49. Complementary studies targeting FOXA1, SWI/SNF and p300 establish that DNA-binding specificity, ATPase cycling and chromatin engagement are also pharmacologically actionable50,51,52. DALTACs build on these principles but produce a distinct pharmacological outcome: rather than recruiting an E3 ligase, degrading a complex component or modulating an individual regulator, a DALTAC bifunctional molecule imposes an additional domain-selective interaction between two members within an existing transcriptional complex, converting the complex into a non-productive state. Our proof-of-concept compound, AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1, targets the AR–p300/CBP complex by repurposing the natural interfaces to block activation of the AR oncogenic enhanceosome. Mechanistically, AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 potently suppresses AR transactivation by disrupting the chromatin landscape at AR-bound enhancer sites, particularly AR/ERG co-bound neo-enhancer sites, as evidenced by reduced cofactor recruitment, loss of histone acetylation marks, and displacement of Pol II. Functionally, this shutdown of AR neo-enhanceosome activity translates into strong antitumour efficacy in AR+ prostate cancer models, underscoring the translational potential of DALTAC-1 as a precision therapeutic agent.

The activity of CIP molecules is founded on formation of a ternary complex between the recruited proteins. Using purified full-length proteins, we showed that DALTAC-1 directly enhances AR–p300 complex formation in the absence of DNA or accessory factors. This association requires simultaneous engagement of both proteins by the intact bifunctional molecule and cannot be reproduced by unlinked ligands or control compounds lacking either AR- or p300-binding activity. The activities of multi-protein transcriptional complexes are governed by finely tuned protein–protein interactions at the sub-domain level53. AR normally recruits transcriptional coactivators primarily through its intrinsically disordered NTD, whereas transcription factors engage distinct regions of p300, including its N- and C-terminal regions, to support histone acetylation and transcriptional activation2,9. Our domain-mapping and interface-mutagenesis studies support a refined model in which DALTAC-1 does not necessarily abolish these native contacts. Rather, it imposes an additional, neomorphic interaction between the AR-LBD and the p300 core region containing the BRD and HAT domain, thereby reorganizing the domain-level engagement within the retained AR–p300 complex. Although the atomic architecture of the ternary complex remains unresolved, owing in part to the large size, conformational flexibility and extensive intrinsically disordered regions of full-length AR and p300, our orthogonal biochemical and cellular data demonstrate a DALTAC-induced binding pattern that is distinct from the basal complex and functionally alters AR–p300/CBP activity. This interaction reprogramming markedly suppresses histone acetylation, including H2BNTac, despite the inability of the p300-binding moiety alone to directly inhibit this modification8. In parallel, DALTAC-1 induces acetylation of the AR-NTD and core components of the AR complex, including SRC2/3 and ARID1A/B4,37,54. Because p300 has previously been shown to acetylate AR primarily within the hinge region under androgen stimulation55, the emergence of AR-NTD acetylation suggests that DALTAC-1 redirects p300 substrate engagement, potentially by bringing the AR-NTD into altered proximity to the p300 HAT domain. This substrate reprogramming distinguishes DALTAC-1 from conventional p300/CBP inhibitors and degraders: unlike BRD inhibitors, it extinguishes enhancer-associated H2BNT acetylation and broadly represses transcription, and unlike PROTAC degraders, it acts independently of ubiquitin–proteasome-mediated target depletion.

Because many oncogenes also have essential roles in normal physiology, their pan-inhibition often causes severe side effects. For example, systemic inhibition of p300/CBP disrupts haematopoiesis and leads to thrombocytopenia13. Thus, achieving lineage-selective targeting of oncogenic pathways is an urgent therapeutic need. Existing approaches such as antibody–drug conjugates deliver cytotoxic payloads selectively to cells that express target surface antigens56. However, their broader applicability is limited by the restricted repertoire of tumour-specific surface markers and, in many cases, by suboptimal pharmacokinetic properties57. By contrast, DALTACs offer a fundamentally distinct strategy, selectively rewiring lineage-specific protein complexes that drive oncogenic transcription. In this study, AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 specifically inhibits the growth of AR+ prostate cancer cells with potency comparable to or better than the p300/CBP degrader CBPD-409 but shows markedly reduced activity in p300/CBP-dependent, AR-negative cancers such as neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma and haematological malignancies8. Notably, in AR-negative cells, DALTAC-1 does not suppress H2BNTac, underscoring that DALTAC-1-mediated inhibition of p300/CBP histone acetylation is context-dependent and conferred by domain reprogramming within AR–p300/CBP complexes.

In summary, we establish DALTACs as a new type of chemical proximity modulators that rewire domain-specific protein interactions to selectively deactivate oncogenic complexes. DALTAC-1 induces formation of an AR–p300–DALTAC-1 ternary complex and reprograms the substrate engagement of p300/CBP, markedly suppressing global histone acetylation while enhancing the acetylation of core components within the AR complex. Consequently, DALTAC-1 reinforces AR–p300/CBP co-occupancy at palindromic ARE loci but disrupts the higher-order assembly of the AR complex and erases histone activation marks at AR neo-enhanceosomes (Fig. 5). This work expands the conceptual framework of induced-proximity therapies beyond degradation and coactivator hijacking, paving the way for the rational design of domain-alteration strategies for precise control of disease-relevant protein complexes.

Right, DALTAC-1 induces a neomorphic interaction between AR and p300/CBP that stabilizes the ternary complex at palindromic AREs and reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, suppressing histone acetylation while increasing acetylation of core AR complex components.
